Lessons.Title: Unit Circle: Sine and Cosine Functions
ExplanationParagraphs: The unit circle x²+y²=1 maps each directed angle t to (cos t,sin t).
The horizontal coordinate is cosine, vertical coordinate sine; both are defined on all real angles and range from−1 to1.
The Pythagorean identity sin²t+cos²t=1 follows from x²+y²=1 and helps find an unknown trig value. The quadrant determines its sign.
Standard special angles 0,π/6,π/4,π/3,π/2 and their symmetric rotations have exact algebraic values.
Reference angles measure the acute angle from terminal side to x-axis. Use reference angle magnitudes and quadrant signs.
A radius r circle has coordinates (r cos t,r sin t). For a unit-circle carousel beginning at north, t=π/2+ωtime.
Independent Cool-down: find sin and cos at 4π/3; find cos if sin=5/13 in quadrantII; and find coordinate on radius5 at angleπ/6.
Independent Try It 1: Point atπ/3 on unit circle.
Independent Try It 2: Find sin,cos of angleπ.
Independent Try It 3: If sin=3/5 in QII, find cos.
Independent Try It 4: Evaluate cos(20°) to4 decimals.
Independent Try It 5: Find reference angle for 315°.
Independent Try It 6: Find sin,cos of 5π/4.
Independent Try It 7: Find point on circle r=4 at210°.

KeyConcepts.Title: Unit-circle coordinates
KeyConcepts.Definition: Point at angle t is (cos t,sin t).

KeyConcepts.Title: Pythagorean identity
KeyConcepts.Rule: Missing component sign depends on quadrant.

KeyConcepts.Title: Reference angle
KeyConcepts.Definition: Acute angle between terminal side and x-axis.

SummaryPoints: Unit circle maps to sine and cosine.
Reference angles provide exact special values.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: cos t is x-coordinate, sin t is y-coordinate.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Take positive square root in quadrantIII/IV without checking sign.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use quadrant before selecting radical sign.
